last_checked.note: 2026-08-27 check: v6.1.0.6 (tag created 2026-08-27T17:47:45Z, commit b5b30f9 dated 2026-08-27T00:39:46Z) vs prior-checked v6.0.0.30 (2026-08-20). One intermediate release (v6.0.0.31, 2026-08-26T16:03:57Z) shipped between checks and was skipped per the skill's stated behavior. Queried from 2026-08-26 (a day before the commit date) to now, a ~2-day window -- raw counts aren't directly comparable to prior runs' longer windows. Used logs/analytics/aggregate (group_by status) for exact status totals (info:101017 warn:174831 error:723 critical:0), and 200-500 line /events/search samples per status for message-pattern breakdown. Rollout confirmed across 8 sampled clusters (production x4 incl. ap1a, staging x1, preset-azure-mpc, 2 customer MPC/GCP clusters incl. flywire, hmetrix); this is a partial sample (page limit), not a full cluster census. Critical count is 0 (down from 12 last run) -- no recurrence of the prior Celery-beat shelve-race crash. Of 723 error-status logs sampled: dominated by authlib deprecation-warning stack-trace fragments (known_noise) and TimeLimitExceeded/SIGKILL Celery timeout noise (known_noise). One NEW low-volume error-classified deprecation notice (4 occurrences, NOT added to known_noise pending more data): 'Legacy static RATELIMIT_APPLICATION override detected; migrate to RATELIMIT_APPLICATION_DEFAULT before 2026-12-31' -- same authlib-style pattern of a Python warning mis-classified as ERROR by the log pipeline; deadline is 4 months out, not urgent. One NEW single-occurrence Celery parse error on a customer's virtual dataset SQL ('Error parsing near 'guardian_id' at line 983:60', SupersetParseError) -- one-off customer query issue, not systemic, NOT added to known_noise. The dominant WARN-status finding: 'Session-invalidation check failed; allowing request' was ~498/500 of the warn sample (and warn total jumped to 174,831, by far the largest share of all logs) -- this is a NEW message string from a new module (superset/security/session_invalidation.py, added this release) that wraps enforce_session_validity(). Inspected exc_info on 3 sample events across 3 different clusters (hmetrix-gcp-mpc, production-aws-ap1a, flywire-aws-mpc): all are flask_jwt_extended.exceptions.NoAuthorizationError: 'Missing JWT in cookies or headers (Missing cookie "__s__"; Missing Authorization Header)' -- i.e. the exact same underlying condition as the pre-existing known_noise entry 'Not authorized Missing JWT in cookies or headers' (health-check/unauthenticated-request probes hitting protected endpoints). The new session-invalidation module fail-opens (allows the request) and logs a WARNING when it can't determine the user's auth state, which for already-unauthenticated traffic is expected, not a security regression. Added 'Session-invalidation check failed; allowing request' to known_noise on this basis. Worth a sanity check next run that the message stays flat/proportional to traffic rather than climbing, and that it's confined to genuinely-unauthenticated routes (not appearing for sessions that should be authenticated).
